title: Eval guardrails: stratified sampling, drift detection, and automated rollback PRD for Optimize
creator: Ava Martinez
description: PRD for end-to-end Eval Guardrails that combine stratified prompt sampling, automated drift detection, and deterministic rollback triggers for the Optimize product. Purpose: prevent quality regressions when recommending batching/quantization/model changes, give PMs & SREs deterministic decision criteria, and enable partially-automated rollbacks with clear human-in-the-loop checkpoints.
scope: Define sampling matrix and sentinel design for production prompt cohorts; specify statistical tests and thresholds for drift/regression; outline A/B criteria for gated rollouts; define automated rollback triggers and human approval gates; implement dashboards and alerting hooks in Console. This PRD covers backend signal definitions and acceptance criteria; instrumentation and UI work will be separate tickets.
out_of_scope: Full UI mockups for Console (handled by design), model retraining pipelines, and per-customer custom thresholding (handled by later enterprise feature). Deep security review of telemetry payloads is a separate ticket.
success_metrics: <1.5% net quality regressions observed in canary rollouts across top-10 customers within first 72h
Time-to-detect drift reduced from median 6h to median <=1h
False-positive automated rollbacks < 5% of automated triggers over 30 days
Coverage: sampled prompt sets represent >= 95% of token volume by cohort after stratification
acceptance_criteria: Sampling: system can generate stratified prompt sets for 6 predefined cohorts (latency-sensitive, cost-sensitive, long-context, short-context, embeddings-heavy, rerank) and export as CSV within the console/playground
Sentinels: team-defined sentinel prompts stored and executed automatically on canary traffic with results visible in dashboard
Drift detection: statistical tests (KS/AD for continuous scores, chi-square for categorical outcomes) and rolling-window comparisons are implemented with configurable window sizes (default 24h, 72h)

Regression thresholds: default thresholds implemented - +5% semantic-accuracy drop (relative), +2% failing-response-rate, +10% tail-latency increase; thresholds must be configurable at project and org level
A/B gating: system supports traffic splits (canary up to 10%) and computes AB metrics with p-value correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) before allowing automated promotion

Rollback triggers: automated rollback executes when composite signal exceeds threshold AND at least one human reviewer has not flagged 'hold' within 15 minutes; automated rollback must log a GitHub PR link and incident ticket
Observability: dashboards show per-signal time series, attribution by cohort, and a drift heatmap; alerts to PagerDuty and Slack with actionable runbook links
E2E tests: synthetic harness reproduces a simulated 7% quality drop and validates that detection + rollback flow fires in CI
promptset_sampling_plan: Stratify sampling by usage tercile (top-10% high-volume, mid 40%, long tail) and by workload type (generation/chat, embeddings, rerank)
Weighted sampling to ensure at least 300 unique prompts per cohort per day for customers >$5k/mo; fallback to pooled corpus for small customers
Include adversarial and edge-case buckets (inputs > 3k tokens, non-UTF8/emoji-heavy, instruction/zero-shot) as at-least-once sentinels
Retention: store sampled prompt sets and model outputs for 90d for regression triage
regression_thresholds: Semantic quality drop: relative decrease >= 5% over baseline (measured by automated eval suite + human-labeled benchmark)
Failing-response-rate: absolute increase >= 2 percentage points for literal errors, hallucinations, or empty outputs
Latency: 95th percentile increase >= 10% or absolute increase > 300ms
Embedding drift: cosine similarity mean shift <= -0.03 relative to baseline cohort
ab_criteria: Minimum sample size: 1k effective events per variant or use Bayesian sequential testing with pre-specified stopping rules
Significance & multiplicity: control false discovery rate using BH correction across the prioritized metric set
Traffic ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 10% over 24h steps if no alerts triggered
Promotion guard: promote only when primary quality metric passes threshold AND no failing sentinels in last 48h
rollback_triggers: Automated: composite signal (weighted sum of normalized metrics) exceeds 1.0 for 3 consecutive evaluation windows (default window=1h)
Manual: SE or PM raises 'urgent regression' with supported evidence (diff, sample traces) and SRE approves rollback
Safety-stop: any sentinel classified as 'critical' (policy-defined) failing even once triggers immediate automated rollback
Cost-trigger: sudden 30% token cost increase without matching throughput increase flags for pause and human review
monitoring_signals: Resource signals: GPU memory pressure, batch sizes, KV cache miss rates
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (internal): run eval guardrails against internal traffic and experimental models for 2 weeks
Stage 2 (pilot): enable for 3 high-volume customers with dedicated alerts; manual review requirement on first two rollbacks
Stage 3 (gradual rollout): enable automatic canaries for all orgs with default thresholds; give each org opt-out and custom thresholding as enterprise feature
Stage 4 (GA): promote to default for new models and Optimize recommendations after 60 days of stable results
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy auto-eval proxies produce false positives -> Mitigation: require sentinel failures or human review for 'critical' rollbacks
Risk: sampling misses rare but important prompts -> Mitigation: periodic targeted sampling of long-tail customers and randomization jitter
Risk: rollback causes thrashing between model variants -> Mitigation: implement cooldown windows (default 24h) and backoff rules
Risk: operator overload from alerts -> Mitigation: prioritize signals, aggregate related alerts, and provide an incidents digest
decisions: Use a composite signal (weighted) for automated rollback rather than single-metric gating to reduce false positives
Default thresholds above are conservative; allow per-org override behind feature flag
Adopt Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the metric set for A/B tests to control FDR
open_questions: Should sentinel severity tiers be user-configurable or platform-defined?
Do we allow customers to opt into automated rollback at org level OR enforce manual approval by default for first 30 days?
What SLA do we commit to for drift detection latency in Dedicated/private deployments with limited telemetry?
